title: Extremely disappointing
body: I found this app on Tik Tok and was curious to give it a try. I have been wanted to stop making boxed lunches and make cheap healthy food. So I was super excited to see that this app said it would teach me not only to cook but to cook cheap since it had a lesson on that. I set my cooking skull up to beginner and started the first lesson My first lesson was “How to Stretch Your Cash”. The lesson was mostly fluff and did not actually teach anything. The main point to ingredients being expensive was don’t buy all of them. That makes little sense when it’s an essential part of the dish. The only useful part was the idea of freezing things. Overall a really disappointing lesson. I still pushed through and hoped that the dish itself was good. The first dish I made was the Teriyaki Salmon and Roasted Broccoli which followed the lesson. First the ingredients were not that cheap. The whole meal ended up costing me $5-7 a plate which is much more expensive compared to $1-2 boxed meals. This was mostly because of the salmon. Second problem was the recipe. I liked all the little tips they had for many parts but it bothered me that it could not make rice correctly. I do know how to make rice and the recipe said to make is differently than I usually do so I tried it. Unfortunately I had to keep adding water because it was not done. This could have been solved if the right amount of rice was added. Lastly the dish itself was bland and had little flavor. The only real flavor added was from the teriyaki sauce which was not nearly enough. I had to add other seasonings I had just to taste anything other than fish. With these disappointments, I thought that maybe it was this particular recipe so I decided to try another. My next lesson was “Cook Better Food Tonight”. It mostly talked about adding salt and browning things. The lesson was slightly more useful than my first one but it did annoy me that there was so much reliance on salt because there are better ways to season food. Nevertheless I started the next recipe, vegetarian green curry. This recipe ended up being slightly cheaper than the previous one at $4-5 but not cheaper than boxed meals. I decided to try and save a little bit by using some spices from another curry recipe on the app instead of buying store bought curry sauce like it wanted me to. The recipe had the same problem as the last one because the rice was not cooked. The taste of the dish was better than the previous one but still pretty bland even with the extra spices. Overall, the app is simply not worth it on all levels. The lessons aren’t great. The recipes are expensive and don’t taste good. And on top of that you can’t even see all the recipes without paying $120 a year. Extremely disappointing.

title: Just started, good features, possibly limited?
body: The format and ease of use of the app is really good. My daughter (14) got into cooking during the pandemic and the one thing she gets annoyed at is when recipes assume she knows how to dice, sauté or judge amounts of ingredients. This learning focused app gives directions on a lot of those things. My daughter and I just downloaded this app yesterday. The lessons were short and clear. I really liked how we could put all the ingredients for the 3 meals in one shopping list and check off what we already had at home. We cooked Aloo Gobi today and the video directions in the recipe were helpful. I think the temperature needed to come down a bit sooner, because the whole bottom of the pan was pretty burnt on, but it didn’t seem to hurt the flavor/texture. We also wanted clearer directions on how much salt. It said a lot, but it also said “sprinkle on salt” a bunch of times and we had different ideas about how much to sprinkle. My husband and I didn’t like the aloo Gobi, it tastes different than in our local Indian restaurant, but my daughter liked it. The raita was new to us and better than we expected. Looking forward to trying more of the recipes. I’m a bit concerned that there aren’t a ton of free ones, but it isn’t clear that a there are a lot more if we pay the monthly fee. But I’m not sure how new the app is and what “coming soon” means in that context. Overall, good idea, well designed, and we’ll certainly be using it more and keeping an eye on when things are added.

title: Impressed

The instructions are very clear and very simple - not intimidating for new (or old 😆) cooks. Also, the instructor in the videos is great teacher! Nice voice and just enough personality to keep it interesting. The recipes even tell you when you have a minute or two to clean up and reset your cooking space! I am not 100 percent sold on the variety/taste of the recipes - I haven’t tried any yet, but I’m not blown away by the selection. Still - I will withhold judgement until I try a few. title: Great to learn the basics- not the tastiest recipes
body: The app does a really good job of teaching the basics of what makes a meal really taste good, and the core principles of each part of the cooking process. Its really funny too, my favorite quote being “Water will never outgrow you or ‘need more space’ Water will be right there, boiling away at 212°F” Stuff like that makes key points really memorable. I enjoy using the app to learn. My only complaint is the options for dishes. Most of them just do not appeal to me. I was expecting to learn more traditional and i suppose for a lack of better words, universally liked meals. Some of choices are really good, like the chimmichuri steak, garlic shrimp scampi, and candied sweet potato fries were really good but… a lot of dishes appeared to be on the blander side of the things. The chicken dishes look unlike what im used to seeing in terms of color. I just opt to season as i please, as the app encourages. I wanted to make a good mac and cheese, the options were disappointing. Im figuring the app aims to make the user learn healthier dishes and choices which is REALLY COOL dont get me wrong. But i want to make meals my entire family will enjoy. The way im using the app now is to learn principles and techniques, and then using this newfound knowledge to make the meals my family will enjoy using youtube videos. Ive gotten really good in a short amount of time. Baked mac and cheese, wings, ribs, burgers, steaks, salmon. I might be good enough by November to be able to throw my hat in the ring for thanksgiving.

title: THE app I’ve been searching for!
body: I’ve been searching for an app that would help inspire me in the kitchen, learn to create new dishes, make shopping for necessary ingredients easy, and to help me prep for each week in advance. THIS. IS. IT!! And then some! The meal planning apps I tried didn’t offer much flexibility and certainly didn’t aim to teach you the “why’s” and “how’s” of cooking. Some did offer the easy shopping options, but none came close to what this app offers me. Tips. Videos. Quizzes. Amazing recipes. The essentials of cooking taught in a humorous and fun manner. I don’t leave many app reviews at all, but this app deserves to be rated, reviewed, and shared a million times over. If you’re the kind of person who shops and buys the same old stuff every time, or who ends up tossing wasted, unused foods that were never cooked, or who sees a pantry full of ingredients but cannot think of a single recipe to make with them, THIS IS FOR YOU! If you just want to expand your knowledge in the kitchen, THIS IS FOR YOU! If you’re just looking for some fresh, new recipes, THIS IS FOR YOU. If you want to understand why or how cutting ingredients a specific way actually matters, THIS IS FOR YOU! If you want to plan out a menu for a week or a month or whatever, and be able to instantly add all required ingredients (and easily remove the ones you don’t need), THIS. IS. FOR. YOU!!! The devs have done such an amazing job with this app, and I am so thrilled that I found it (completely by accident, mind you) on the App Store. Big thank yous to all who worked on this app! I look forward to saving money, not wasting food anymore, knowing exactly what I need for my planned menus, and understanding why I’m cooking things a certain way. I look so forward to being more of a chef and less of a not-so-confident home cook. 😁

title: Yay I can cook now (only took me 100 years)
body: So far I like this app. I'm only using the free version and I've only made mac n cheese- but it managed to make some pretty good mac n cheese. My mom liked it too(and not in the fake mom way, she was grabbing herself seconds n thirds n everything) I love the teaching style, I love the little classes that teach about organics. If the second recipe comes out good as well I may even start paying for the service. However, I think it could use some improvements? Mostly in the search section, I often try to find things to no avail. I saw lemonade the other day so I search "Drinks" out of curiosity. Nothing pops up. The categories help but sometimes things that look like they should be in a category.... aren't. It's not a huge thing and I'm only level 2. Maybe adding a way to sort by levels would help? All the level one foods disappeared when I leveled up and now I have to use the search system to find them :/ Also maybe if I level up level one foods shouldn't give as many points? Or just recipes I've done before maybe? On duoling if you repeat a lesson you only get five points. The point isn't to shame anyone but I can't really see how cooking mac n cheese 100 times would make me level five worthy. I mean it could? I could be a mac n cheese master or something. But!!! If someone reading this is thinking about downloading the app you should def give it a try. I've always had problems with cooking anything at all and I've learnt more here than I have from my mother, grandma, cooking teachers, cook books, podcasts, youtubers, or anyone else. It's nice to be able to learn at my own pace.

title: Genuinely excited
body: Having just cooked my first meal with this app, I feel I can say I’m very excited for where I’ll go with it! I’ve long been looking for something this accessible to help me learn and feel more comfortable with cooking. I think I can say that I’ve found that with Zest. The wealth of knowledge available in each recipe really makes you feel at ease with each recipe, with bite-sized tips and tricks through videos within the steps. I love the broad range of recipes even separated by your skill level, with more complex dishes and simple single-digit ingredient dishes all available even at my introductory skill level. This move was genius, I think, because having that rush of being able to make something delicious and quick but also learning as I go will definitely help keep me engaged! I honestly can’t wait to explore more recipes and learn more, I already have a dozen recipes saved! Addition to my previous review after using it for a while longer: I love this app for how it has helped me cook for my family a lot more than I used to in my pre-Zest days! One gripe and suggestion for a clarification to add for equipment: I have many times not used the right sized bowl or pan or pot. Saying “small” or “large” is not always specific enough. A suggested volume of size would be immensely helpful! In fact, I would love to see a View Details option for the Equipment section in the future.

title: I put way too much effort into this review
body: I’m only one lesson in but I’m already obsessed. I live alone which is awesome ✨except for cooking✨ because no one makes recipes for one person! Dividing a recipe up takes math, cooking the whole thing creates leftovers I never eat, etc. This app lets you automatically set the recipe for one person. (Shout out to creators and developers who understand single person households exist lol.) It also tells you what order to prep in rather than just giving you the list, which will help me avoid doing things in the wrong order or starting to cook pasta sauce before realizing I don’t have XYZ ingredient and now I have to mince some garlic at the speed of light without chopping off a finger. I was quite literally crying the other night as I was looking for cooking classes, which also don’t exist for one person, apparently, for anything less than $90. Was I doomed to be a bad cook living off Bagel Bites and Kraft even as an adult? I was certain, in my hunger and empty fridge-fueled breakdown, that this was so. Then, like Gandalf arriving at Helm’s Deep on the first light of the fifth day, Zest appeared when all hope was lost. It’s like if the show Salt Fat Acid Heat was an app. It’s a cooking class that doesn’t require you to leave your house or embarrass yourself in front of strangers or be the 7th wheel in a couple’s cooking class. And the recipes so far are simple and don’t require 7,348 pots and dishes, but somehow also teach you how to cook. I just compared this app to Gandalf so needless to say I will likely buy premium because there is no other app like this that I’ve found. Hats (specifically chef hats) off to you, dev.
